feature.title: Enhanced graphics mode for the dancing character
feature.request:
from origin/main, plan the following: <task>
-add support for an 'enhanced graphics' version of the dancing-character visualization
</task>

<context>
-Right now, we are optimizing for low-quality laptops and computers. This is fine, but we should let users that want a prettier looking visualization with solid setups to get a more impressive experience
</context>

<requirements>
-We should offer a more visually-stunning option for those with more memory, CPU, and GPU power
-This can include high-quality skyboxes, reflective surfaces, complex textures, and whatever else would enhance a visualization
-By default, it will be turned off, but the setting should be easily accessible and viewable so people know it exists quickly.  We should also store their selection in cookies so it stays enabled between sessions
</requirements>

<scope-and-non-goals>
-don't fundamentally change any visualizations structurally. it should simply enhance what we already have with better textures, lighting, etc
</scope-and-non-goals>

problem.statement: The dancing-character visualizer is tuned for low-end laptops (no antialias, no shadows, no tone mapping, flat colour background, simple lights). Users with capable machines have no way to opt into a richer look, and nobody can discover that such an option exists.
users: Users on capable desktops or gaming laptops who want a more impressive dancer scene
Users on low-end laptops who must keep today's performance unchanged by default
evidence: useDancingCharacterScene calls useThreeScene with defaults: antialias off, pixel ratio capped at 2 (context brief)
dancingCharacterScene.ts sets no shadows or tone mapping; club owns a flat #07080f background and matching fog
No persisted app-wide setting exists; storage.ts uses localStorage audioVisualizer.* keys

goals: An app-wide Enhanced graphics preference, off by default, persisted in localStorage across sessions
The preference is visible on the landing page and in the dancing-character control panel

When on, the dancing character renders with richer lighting, shadows, environment reflections, a reflective floor, an HQ sky/backdrop and better textures and antialiasing, without structural scene changes
A non-binding capability hint and a slow-frame-rate notice help users choose sensibly
non_goals: Structural changes to any visualization (choreography, layout, reactions to audio, controls other than the new toggle)
Enhanced modes for visualizers other than dancing-character in this plan (the preference is app-wide so they can opt in later)
Automatically enabling or disabling enhanced mode
Upgrading three.js or adding non-addon rendering dependencies
success_metrics: Standard mode is byte-for-byte unchanged in rendering setup and its GLB/JS download for users who never opt in (enhanced code and assets lazy-loaded)
Enhanced toggle discoverable from the landing page without opening a visualizer
Bundle-size and Lighthouse budgets pass, or any increase is justified in the PR
Toggling enhanced mode on and off repeatedly leaks no WebGL contexts or GPU resources (e2e context count stable)
constraints: three.js r186 pinned; only three/addons may be used
Named exports, logic outside React, no React state in the render loop, every GPU resource disposed, no per-frame allocation (AGENTS.md rules)
Use useThreeScene, disposeScene, useControlValues/ControlPanel; follow the cubes RoomEnvironment+PMREM pattern
Changing antialias rebuilds the renderer via useThreeScene deps; the e2e fixture fails on too many WebGL contexts
95% coverage over app/**; visual baselines for the settings panel and landing page will change and need the Update visual snapshots workflow
.size-limit.json Total JS counts lazy chunks; new assets must be credited in assets/CREDITS.md with compatible licenses (CC0 preferred)
Asset bytes for enhanced mode are only fetched when enhanced mode is on

acceptance_criteria.given: a first-time visitor with empty localStorage
acceptance_criteria.then: Enhanced graphics shows as off on the landing page and in the control panel, and the scene renders exactly as today with no enhanced assets requested

acceptance_criteria.given: a visitor on the landing page
acceptance_criteria.when: they look at the page without scrolling past the cards header
acceptance_criteria.then: an Enhanced graphics toggle with a short description is visible and operable by keyboard and screen reader (accessible name and state)

acceptance_criteria.given: the user turns Enhanced graphics on (landing page or control panel)
acceptance_criteria.when: they reload or return in a new session
acceptance_criteria.then: the setting is still on, read from localStorage key audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphics, and both surfaces show the same state

it uses antialiasing, AgX or neutral tone mapping on lit materials only (LED tiles, seams and beam cones stay toneMapped false and keep their colours), soft shadows from the key light cast by every loaded character onto a ShadowMaterial catcher just above the LED floor, a PMREM environment lighting the character and frame, a low-opacity glass reflection layer over the tiles that lets the LED pattern show through, and a dark sky dome (fog false) whose horizon matches the fog colour; existing club meshes, character, dances, camera and audio reactions are unchanged

acceptance_criteria.given: the dancing character page is open
acceptance_criteria.when: the user toggles Enhanced graphics on and off five times, including while enhanced assets are still loading
acceptance_criteria.then: the scene switches mode without a page reload, the camera pose is kept, the e2e WebGL context count stays within the fixture limit, any asset that finishes loading after teardown is disposed, and the console shows no errors or context warnings

acceptance_criteria.given: the browser exposes WebGL2 with MAX_TEXTURE_SIZE of at least 8192, and the optional signals (deviceMemory of at least 8, hardwareConcurrency of at least 8, unmasked renderer not software) pass wherever they are available
acceptance_criteria.when: the user sees the toggle while it is off
acceptance_criteria.then: a small 'your device can likely handle this' hint appears; it never changes the setting, it is absent when a required signal fails, and the probe runs after idle and releases its context so the landing page has zero live WebGL contexts

acceptance_criteria.given: Enhanced graphics is on and, after a warm-up that restarts on every rebuild and asset swap, the frame rate stays below the threshold over the window while the tab is visible (frames with a capped-out dt are ignored)
acceptance_criteria.then: a dismissible notice, shown inside the fullscreen wrapper so it is visible in fullscreen, offers to switch back to standard; the setting changes only if the user accepts, and after dismissal it does not reappear for the rest of the page visit, even across rebuilds

acceptance_criteria.given: localStorage is unavailable or holds an invalid value
acceptance_criteria.then: it falls back to off without throwing, matching storage.ts error handling

acceptance_criteria.given: Enhanced graphics is on and the enhanced module or an enhanced asset fails to load
acceptance_criteria.then: the scene keeps rendering the standard look, the toggle status reads 'Could not load enhanced assets, using standard', one console warning is logged, and the stored preference stays on

acceptance_criteria.given: the app is open in two tabs
acceptance_criteria.when: the preference is changed in one tab
acceptance_criteria.then: the other tab's toggles reflect the new value via the storage event

decisions.question: Scope of the setting
decisions.answer: App-wide Enhanced graphics preference, surfaced on the landing page and in the visualizer control panel; only dancing-character consumes it initially, others may opt in later.

decisions.question: Persistence mechanism
decisions.answer: localStorage instead of a cookie (same persistence across sessions, nothing sent with requests, matches existing app storage).

decisions.question: Capability detection
decisions.answer: Default stays off; show a non-binding 'your device can likely handle this' hint when a capability heuristic passes.

decisions.question: Behavior when enhanced mode is slow
decisions.answer: After sustained low frame rate, show a dismissible notice offering to switch back; never change the setting without the user.

decisions.question: Framing confirmation
decisions.answer: Problem, goals, non-goals and ACs confirmed as written.

decisions.question: Enhanced backdrop style
decisions.answer: Richer dark club: keep the night-club mood with a high-res dark environment (haze, light shafts, dusky or starry sky dome), not a photographic daylight skybox.

decisions.question: Extra download budget for enhanced mode
decisions.answer: Up to about 30 MB, fetched only when enhanced mode is on (allows 4K HDR environment and high-res PBR textures).

decisions.question: Where persistence lives
decisions.answer: Extend the existing localStorage pattern in app/features/audio/storage.ts style with key audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphics; no cookie code.
decisions.rationale: storage.ts is the only persistence and swallows storage errors

decisions.question: Toggle mode-switch mechanism
decisions.answer: A toggle rebuilds the scene through useThreeScene (antialias dep); EnhancedLook only disposes what it created (no restore), takes an AbortSignal, and the camera pose is kept in a ref across the rebuild.
decisions.rationale: Critic F4: the rebuild already frees renderer state

decisions.question: Asset format and size
decisions.answer: 2K RGBE HDR for lighting (PMREM), 4K LDR sky texture for the dome, PBR floor maps at 2K; every file under 20 MiB (Workers caps a single asset at 25 MiB); the total stays under about 30 MB.
decisions.rationale: Critic F8: per-file Workers limit and decode stall

decisions.question: Rollout of the visible toggle
decisions.answer: The store and toggle ship in S1 but the toggle UI is behind a constant (ENHANCED_GRAPHICS_UI) that is on in dev and turned on for production in S3, once the enhanced look is complete.
decisions.rationale: Critic F6: avoid a misleading control

options.summary: Add a tiny shared enhancedGraphics store (localStorage + useSyncExternalStore), one toggle on landing page and in the dancer panel, and a lazily imported enhanced module that applies tone mapping, shadows, PMREM env, reflective floor and HDR backdrop to the existing scene; antialias flips via useThreeScene deps.
approach: Add app/features/graphics/enhancedGraphics.ts: read/write key audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphics (try/catch, invalid -> false), subscribe, plus useEnhancedGraphics hook via useSyncExternalStore so landing page and panel share state.

Add EnhancedGraphicsToggle (role=switch, accessible name, description) used on the landing page header and as a panel row in DancingCharacterPage; show capability hint from pure canUseEnhanced(gl caps, deviceMemory, hardwareConcurrency) when off.
useDancingCharacterScene passes antialias: enhanced to useThreeScene; renderer rebuild is the mode switch, so no reload and the existing forceContextLoss teardown keeps context count stable.

Add dancingCharacterEnhanced.ts, dynamically imported only when on: sets toneMapping, shadowMap PCFSoft, key light shadows, RoomEnvironment/HDR PMREM env, MeshReflectorMaterial-free reflective floor via addons Reflector, dark HDR backdrop; returns dispose().
Lazy-load HDR and PBR textures from assets/ via ?url inside that module; credit them in assets/CREDITS.md.
Add useFpsWatch (ring counter in existing loop, no allocation) raising a dismissible notice once per page visit; accept calls setEnhancedGraphics(false).
Unit tests per file for 95% coverage; one e2e toggle loop; update visual snapshots.
contracts: getEnhancedGraphics(): boolean; setEnhancedGraphics(v: boolean): void; useEnhancedGraphics(): boolean
applyEnhanced(renderer, scene, club, light): Promise<{ dispose(): void }>
pros: Reuses useThreeScene rebuild, cubes PMREM pattern, storage.ts style
Standard path untouched; assets fetched only when on
cons: Mode switch reloads character via renderer rebuild
Control-panel placement needs a custom row, not a control table entry
Lazy chunk adds to Total JS size limit
risks: Reflector floor and 4K HDR may be slow under SwiftShader e2e
Context count near fixture limit on rapid toggling
Disposal of env, reflector and shadow maps must be complete

options.summary: A validated, subscribable app-wide preference store plus a lazily imported EnhancedLook module that a rebuilt-on-toggle dancer scene applies and fully disposes, with pure capability and frame-rate classes and a guaranteed fall-back to standard on any load failure.
approach: Add enhancedGraphicsStore (pure module, localStorage key audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphics, strict 'true'/'false' parse, try/catch like storage.ts, in-memory fallback, same-tab listeners plus 'storage' event) exposed to React via useSyncExternalStore in useEnhancedGraphics; landing page and panel both subscribe so they always agree.

Add a shared EnhancedGraphicsToggle (role=switch, aria-checked, described-by text, optional capability hint) used on the landing header and as the first ControlPanel row of the dancing-character table; the control is outside valuesRef.
useDancingCharacterScene passes antialias: enhanced to useThreeScene, so a toggle rebuilds renderer, scene and character with forceContextLoss on teardown (no reload, stable context count).

Standard path never imports enhanced code. Enhanced path does import('./enhanced/dancingCharacterEnhanced') inside setup behind a cancelled-flag; the module returns an EnhancedLook with apply(scene, renderer, club) and dispose().

EnhancedLook sets ACES tone mapping, PCFSoft shadow map on the key light, PMREM env from a lazy 4K HDR dark-club asset (temp scene and loader disposed), a Reflector/MeshReflectorMaterial-style floor overlay, a dome backdrop, and upgraded textures with anisotropy; it records originals and restores them in dispose.
On any import or asset failure, log once, keep standard rendering, show an inline error notice, and never alter the stored preference.

Pure detectCapability(probe) and FrameRateMonitor (fixed ring buffer, no per-frame allocation, sustained-window threshold) drive the hint (AC6) and the dismissible once-per-visit notice (AC7); accepting calls the store setter.

options.summary: One shared, accessible Enhanced graphics switch (landing page and control panel) backed by a tiny external store, with explicit loading, failure, hint and slow-FPS states so toggling never looks broken or surprising.
approach: enhancedGraphicsStore.ts: pure get/set/subscribe over localStorage audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphics (invalid or unavailable -> off, errors swallowed); consumed via useSyncExternalStore so landing page, panel and scene always agree, including across tabs via the storage event.

EnhancedGraphicsToggle component: role=switch button with accessible name, aria-checked, visible On/Off text, description linked by aria-describedby; placed in the landing header above the cards and as the first row of the dancer ControlPanel, reusing the same component.

Status line (aria-live polite) under the toggle: 'Loading enhanced assets...' while fetching, 'Enhanced graphics on', or 'Could not load enhanced assets, using standard' on failure (store reverts to off only for the session, not persisted).

Scene keeps rendering the standard look while enhanced assets load, then swaps in the environment, floor and sky in one frame, so there is no blank canvas and no reload; antialias change rebuilds the renderer with the existing useThreeScene path, showing the page's current loading overlay.

capabilityHint.ts: pure heuristic (WebGL2, max texture size, non-software renderer, deviceMemory, hardwareConcurrency) run once on idle; renders 'Your device can likely handle this' text only while off and only on pass; never writes the store.

frameRateMonitor.ts: rolling average sampled in the existing loop without allocation; after sustained low FPS raises a dismissible, non-modal notice (role=status) with 'Switch to standard' and 'Dismiss' buttons, focus not stolen; dismissal held in a module flag for the page visit.
Lazy enhanced module (dynamic import) holds PMREM env, HDR, PBR floor, shadows and tone mapping; disposed fully on toggle off.
contracts: detectCapability(): boolean (false when it cannot run)
pros: Consistent state and wording on both surfaces
Every state (loading, error, slow, success) is communicated and keyboard and screen-reader operable
No reload or blank flash when switching
cons: New shared component and settings folder add more surface than a panel-only toggle
Landing page and panel visual baselines both change
risks: Renderer rebuild on antialias flip may flash the loading overlay
Cross-tab storage event handling adds test burden for 95% coverage
FPS thresholds can false-trigger on software WebGL in e2e

options.summary: Hybrid of O2 and O3: O2's validated subscribable store, restore-on-dispose EnhancedLook lazy module and fall-back-on-failure, with O3's single shared accessible toggle, aria-live loading/error status, standard look kept until enhanced assets are ready, and non-modal slow-FPS notice. Sources: O2 (store, EnhancedLook, pure capability and FrameRateMonitor classes), O3 (toggle component, states, no-blank swap).
approach: enhancedGraphicsStore in app/features/settings/: get/set/subscribe over localStorage audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphics, strict 'true'/'false' parse, errors swallowed, same-tab listeners plus the storage event; useEnhancedGraphics via useSyncExternalStore.

Shared EnhancedGraphicsToggle (role=switch, aria-checked, visible On/Off, aria-describedby description, optional hint, aria-live status) in the landing header above the cards and as a row at the top of the dancer ControlPanel, outside valuesRef and the control table.

useDancingCharacterScene passes antialias: enhanced to useThreeScene (existing rebuild path with forceContextLoss); setup dynamically imports enhanced/dancingCharacterEnhanced only when on, behind a cancelled flag.

EnhancedLook.apply(ctx) sets ACES tone mapping and sRGB output, PCFSoft shadows from the key light onto the floor, a PMREM environment (RoomEnvironment immediately, then a lazy dark-club HDR when loaded), a Reflector-based floor overlay, a dark sky dome with stars and haze, and anisotropic or PBR textures; it records every mutated property and restores and frees it in dispose().
Standard look renders first; enhanced assets swap in when loaded. On import or asset failure: log once, keep standard, show an error status, do not change the stored preference.

Pure detectCapability(probe) drives the hint; FrameRateMonitor (fixed ring buffer, sustained window, warm-up ignored) drives a dismissible once-per-visit SlowFrameNotice whose accept calls setEnhancedGraphics(false).

components.name: EnhancedLook
components.responsibility: lazy apply and full restore of enhanced rendering

pros: Leak-free toggling by construction plus every user-visible state covered
Standard path imports no enhanced code or assets
Pure classes are easy to cover to 95%
cons: Antialias toggle rebuilds the renderer and reloads the character (brief overlay)
More files than the minimal option
Lazy chunk counts toward Total JS
risks: Software-WebGL e2e slowness with shadows, reflector and HDR
Reflector floor may clash with the club floor
Large HDR download needs visible loading state

decision_rationale: O4 keeps O2's restore-on-dispose and failure fallback, which protect AC5 and AC8, and adds O3's loading, error, hint and notice states, which the discoverability and slow-FPS decisions (D1, D3, D4) need. That costs about M, between O1 and O2. O1 is cheaper but leaves the loading and failure states undefined with a 30 MB asset budget.

design.overview: An app-wide enhanced-graphics preference (localStorage, off by default) is read through a subscribable store by a shared toggle on the landing page and in a new optional header slot of the dancer's ControlPanel. When it is on, the dancer scene is rebuilt with antialias, and an EnhancedLook layer is lazily applied on top of the unchanged club, character and dances: tone mapping on lit materials only, a shadow catcher, a PMREM environment, a low-opacity glass reflection layer, a dark sky dome and upgraded character materials. Turning it off rebuilds the standard scene exactly as today.

components.name: EnhancedGraphicsToggle
components.responsibility: accessible switch with description, hint and status

components.name: EnhancedLook
components.responsibility: apply and restore all enhanced renderer and scene changes; owns its GPU resources

components.name: enhanced assets
components.responsibility: dark-club HDR, floor PBR textures, credited

components.name: FrameRateMonitor + SlowFrameNotice
components.responsibility: sustained low-FPS detection and dismissible offer

contracts.name: enhancedGraphicsStore
contracts.definition: getEnhancedGraphics(): boolean (false on missing, invalid or unavailable storage); setEnhancedGraphics(on: boolean): void (writes 'true'/'false', notifies listeners, swallows storage errors); subscribeEnhancedGraphics(cb): () => void (also fires on the window storage event for the key); key audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphics

contracts.name: EnhancedLook
contracts.definition: createEnhancedLook(ctx: { renderer, scene, club, keyLight, framing, signal: AbortSignal, onStatus(status: 'loading'|'ready'|'error') }): EnhancedLook; apply(): void sets renderer tone mapping and shadow map, marks club tile, seam and cone materials toneMapped false, adds the shadow catcher, glass reflection layer (half-resolution Reflector, resolution from config) and sky dome, and starts asset loads; onModelChanged(model): void sets castShadow, envMapIntensity and texture anisotropy on the new character's materials and fits the key light's shadow camera to framing, and is called from setCharacter for every load; dispose(): void frees every env map, render target, texture, geometry and material it created, including assets that resolve after abort; it does not restore renderer state because the toggle rebuilds the renderer

contracts.name: detectCapability
contracts.definition: detectCapability(probe: { webgl2: boolean; maxTextureSize: number; renderer?: string; deviceMemory?: number; hardwareConcurrency?: number }): boolean; required: webgl2 and maxTextureSize at least 8192; optional fields fail the check only when present and below threshold (deviceMemory under 8, hardwareConcurrency under 8, renderer matching SwiftShader or llvmpipe). probeCapability() creates a canvas-less context after requestIdleCallback, reads the fields and calls WEBGL_lose_context

contracts.name: FrameRateMonitor
contracts.definition: new FrameRateMonitor({ thresholdFps, windowMs, warmupMs, maxDtMs }); sample(dtMs, hidden): boolean returns true once when the average over the window stays below the threshold after warm-up, ignoring hidden frames and dt above maxDtMs; restartWarmup() is called on every rebuild and asset swap; fixed-size buffer, no per-frame allocation. Dismissal state lives in a module flag for the page visit

contracts.name: ControlPanel header slot
contracts.definition: ControlPanel accepts optional header?: ReactNode rendered above the sections; default none, so other visualizers render unchanged

design.data: One localStorage key, audioVisualizer.enhancedGraphics, values 'true' or 'false'. No cookies, nothing sent to a server.
design.ux: The landing header shows a labelled switch 'Enhanced graphics' with the description 'Richer lighting, reflections and sky for the dancing character. Needs a strong GPU; downloads up to about 30 MB.' The same component sits in the dancer ControlPanel's header slot. While it is off and the heuristic passes, it shows 'Your device can likely handle this'. Status text: Loading enhanced assets / Enhanced graphics on / Could not load enhanced assets, using standard. The slow-FPS notice is non-modal, inside the fullscreen wrapper, with Switch to standard and Dismiss. The camera pose is kept across the toggle; the dance restarts.
design.accessibility: role=switch with aria-checked, accessible name and aria-describedby; status via aria-live polite; the notice uses role=status and never steals focus; all keyboard operable; axe checks in e2e stay clean.
design.security_privacy: Stores only a boolean in localStorage; no tracking, no cookie, no network beyond same-origin static assets. The capability probe reads the WebGL renderer string locally and never sends it anywhere.
design.observability: Console warning once on enhanced import or asset failure (no errors, so e2e fixtures stay green); the existing PerformanceStats toggle lets users and devs see FPS in enhanced mode.
design.rollout: Ships off by default and, until S3, with the toggle UI hidden in production behind ENHANCED_GRAPHICS_UI, so no user sees an incomplete feature. Each slice is merged in order and is independently verifiable in dev. Rollback is a Cloudflare rollback or reverting the PR; a stored 'true' with the code reverted is ignored.

test_strategy.unit: Store parse, fallback, subscribe and storage event; detectCapability matrix (required versus optional fields, SwiftShader, masked renderer); probe releases its context; FrameRateMonitor warm-up, restartWarmup, hidden and dt cap, once-only; EnhancedLook against the fake renderer: tile/seam/cone toneMapped false, onModelChanged on two successive models, dispose frees everything created, and an HDR load resolving after abort is disposed; parse the committed HDR header (dimensions) and assert every enhanced asset file is under 20 MiB; toggle component (jsdom) for role, state, hint and status; ControlPanel header slot default none.
test_strategy.integration: DancingCharacterPage with injected engine and tracker: toggling rebuilds the scene with antialias and keeps the camera pose; the enhanced module import failing keeps standard, shows the error status and leaves the stored value on.
test_strategy.e2e: New spec: landing toggle visible and keyboard operable, and the landing page leaves zero live WebGL contexts after the probe; the state persists across reload and matches the panel; with the real enhanced assets, enabling enhanced mode renders a non-blank canvas with no console errors; toggling on and off five times (once mid-load) keeps the WebGL context count within the fixture limit; standard mode requests no enhanced asset URLs (network listener). No production test seam for reduced assets. Update the visual baselines for the landing page and the dancer settings panel only.
test_strategy.manual: npm run dev on a strong GPU and a weak laptop: side-by-side checklist (LED floor colours unchanged, beam cone intensity unchanged, dark-club mood kept, dancer shadow present for every character), measure the HDR decode stall and GPU memory, check the hint and the slow notice in windowed and fullscreen modes, console clean.
test_strategy.non_functional: npm run size after S2 and after S3 (Total JS budget; justify lazy-chunk growth in the PR); npm run lighthouse on / (the store and toggle import no three.js; the probe runs after idle); enhanced assets total at most about 30 MB and each file under 20 MiB.

CC0 only (for example Poly Haven), sha256 and source in CREDITS.md

Which CC0 dark HDR and floor texture set best fits the club look

findings.finding: AC4 and S2 promise soft shadows onto the floor and a reflective floor, but the real floor (dancingCharacterClub.ts) is an InstancedMesh of MeshBasicMaterial LED tiles recoloured every frame, over a MeshBasicMaterial seams plane. Unlit materials never receive shadows, so the shadow requirement cannot be met on the existing floor. A Reflector 'overlay' on top of the tiles either hides the LED pattern (a structural change, which the non-goals forbid) or z-fights with it. Reflector also re-renders the whole scene a second time per frame, including the per-frame instanceColor upload and additive cones, which doubles the cost on exactly the machines the slow-FPS notice (AC7) is meant to protect. The plan names the clash only as risk K4 and Q2 and never decides how the floors coexist.
findings.suggestion: Before S2, decide the floor treatment explicitly. For example, add a ShadowMaterial catcher plane just above the tiles and a low-opacity, low-resolution Reflector below the tiles' glass layer. State in AC4 which existing meshes are touched. Add a reflector resolution and a toggle-off path to C2.
findings.resolution: Changed: AC4 and C2 now use a ShadowMaterial catcher above the LED tiles and a low-opacity, half-resolution glass reflection layer that lets the tiles show through; existing tile meshes are only marked toneMapped false. The reflector cost is accepted for an opt-in strong-machine mode, and the slow notice covers weak machines.

findings.finding: C2 createEnhancedLook({renderer, scene, club, keyLight}) has no hook for the character model. The model loads asynchronously and again on every character change (useDancingCharacterScene loadCharacter -> character.setCharacter, which clones materials). Nothing in C2 sets castShadow on the new SkinnedMesh, fits the key light's shadow camera to the model framing (dancingCharacterFraming), or applies envMapIntensity or anisotropic or PBR texture upgrades to the new materials. The plan says S2 edits dancingCharacterScene.ts but the contract does not carry it. Result: the dancer casts no shadow, or only the first character does, and 'better textures' (AC4 goal) silently never reach the character.
findings.suggestion: Add an onModelChanged(model) (or a model-visitor) entry to C2, called from setCharacter. State that EnhancedLook re-applies shadow and material settings there, and include it in the S2 unit tests with the fake renderer.
findings.resolution: Changed: C2 adds onModelChanged(model), called from setCharacter for every load, which sets castShadow, envMapIntensity and anisotropy and fits the shadow camera to the framing; S2 unit tests cover two successive models.

findings.finding: Tone mapping is applied renderer-wide, so ACES also affects the MeshBasicMaterial LED tiles, the additive beam cones, the frame and any untoned material. The club's saturated rainbow floor and flashes are the signature look. ACES desaturates and compresses highlights, and a PMREM environment lights the MeshStandardMaterial frame and the character, changing the 'deliberate mood'. K4 says only 'tint and fog keep config colours' plus manual review. The sky dome also needs fog:false and must replace the shared background/fog colour (dancingCharacterConfig background and fog share one colour), which the plan does not specify. Without a rule, AC4's 'club layout and audio reactions unchanged' fails in practice.
findings.suggestion: Set toneMapped:false on tile, cone and seam materials (or use AgX or neutral tone mapping at low exposure), keep fog colour tied to the dome horizon, and add a manual side-by-side checklist item for the LED floor colours and cone intensity.
findings.resolution: Changed: AC4 and C2 use AgX or neutral tone mapping with tiles, seams and cones toneMapped false; the dome has fog false and its horizon matches the fog colour; the manual checklist covers LED colours and cone intensity.

findings.finding: The design is internally inconsistent about what a toggle does. The mode switch is a full useThreeScene rebuild (antialias dep): renderer.dispose, forceContextLoss, disposeScene and a new renderer, scene and character. That already frees everything, so C2's 'record and restore every mutated renderer/scene property' (K5 mitigation, S2 size M, S3 size L) is dead weight for the toggle path, and K5's 'leaves tone mapping on after toggling off' cannot happen because the renderer is new. The real leak risks are different. Async work that outlives teardown (HDR fetch, decode, PMREM finishing after the abort signal) is not covered by the cancelled flag alone, because loaders cannot be aborted. Also, the rebuild loses the user's dragged camera pose and restarts the dance, and may flash the overlay. Tests and effort are aimed at the wrong risk.
findings.suggestion: Drop restore-on-dispose and keep dispose-created-resources only. Make the key AC5 test 'resolve the HDR load after teardown and assert the texture is disposed', and pass the signal into EnhancedLook. Document that the camera pose resets on toggle, or hold it in a ref across the rebuild.
findings.resolution: Changed: D9 and C2 drop restore-on-dispose and keep dispose-created with an AbortSignal; AC5 and the unit tests cover a late HDR resolve; the camera pose is kept across the rebuild.

findings.finding: The toggle needs to be 'a row at the top of the dancer ControlPanel, outside valuesRef and the control table', but ControlPanel (app/components/ControlPanel/ControlPanel.tsx) is shared by every visualizer and takes only definitions and a fixed set of props. No slot or prop exists, and no ControlPanel path appears in any slice's draft_paths. Changing it touches all visualizers' tests and their settings-panel visual baselines, contradicting the plan's claim that only the landing and dancer baselines change. The panel is also hidden during fullscreen (`hidden={fullscreenActive}`), as is anything outside the fullscreen wrapper, so the SlowFrameNotice (AC7) is never seen when a user runs the dancer fullscreen, which is the typical case for a showcase mode.
findings.suggestion: Add S1 work to extend ControlPanel with an optional header slot (default none) and list it in draft_paths and the baseline estimate. Decide the notice placement inside fullscreenRef (and a fullscreen-safe wording) or state that it will not show in fullscreen.
findings.resolution: Changed: new contract C5 (an optional ControlPanel header slot, default none, so other baselines stay unchanged) added to S1 draft_paths; the slow notice is placed inside the fullscreen wrapper (AC7).

findings.finding: S1 ships a user-visible toggle with the description 'Richer lighting, reflections and sky ... downloads up to about 30 MB' while 'enhanced on only switches antialias'. The rollout says each slice is independently shippable, but S1 alone delivers a misleading control and AC1/AC2/AC3 pass vacuously. S4 and S5 depend on different slices (S1, S2), and S5 (FrameRateMonitor in the loop) also needs the enhanced scene to exist. Nothing says the toggle is hidden or flagged until S3 lands, and the status states and failure fallback (loading, error, 'Could not load', unchanged stored value) appear in no acceptance criterion, only in S3's objective.
findings.suggestion: Gate the toggle UI (not the store) behind a build constant until S3 merges, or reword the S1 copy. Add an AC for the load and failure states (HDR 404 or abort keeps standard, shows the status, leaves the stored value on) and an AC for the cross-tab storage event.
findings.resolution: Changed: D11 puts the toggle UI behind ENHANCED_GRAPHICS_UI until S3; added AC9 for the load and failure states and AC10 for cross-tab sync.

findings.finding: AC6 and C3 conflict. AC6 says the hint passes on thresholds 'where available' for deviceMemory and hardwareConcurrency, but C3 returns false when any required field is unknown. deviceMemory exists only in Chromium, and WEBGL_debug_renderer_info is masked in Firefox and Safari, so the hint would effectively never show outside Chromium, or the 'software renderer' check is blind. The probe itself needs a throwaway WebGL context on the landing page (which currently loads no three.js and sits under Lighthouse), and in e2e a context counted by the fixture that is not forceContextLoss'ed. The plan does not say how the probe context is created and released, or that it runs on idle without hurting Lighthouse. Maximum texture size of 'high' is not defined either (Q1 defers thresholds).
findings.suggestion: Define which fields are required (webgl2 and maxTextureSize) versus optional, make C3 match AC6, specify a canvas-less probe that calls WEBGL_lose_context, and run it only after idle. Add an e2e assertion that the landing page leaves zero live contexts.
findings.resolution: Changed: AC6 and C3 now agree (webgl2 and maxTextureSize of at least 8192 are required; the optional fields fail only when present); the probe runs after idle, needs no canvas, calls WEBGL_lose_context, and e2e asserts zero live contexts on the landing page.

findings.finding: D7 (about 30 MB, '4K HDR environment and high-res PBR textures') is decided as a download budget, but the plan never checks that it fits delivery and runtime. wrangler.jsonc serves build/client via Workers static assets, and Cloudflare caps a single asset at 25 MiB. A 4K .hdr from the usual CC0 sources is commonly in that range, so one file can break the deploy. A 4096x2048 float HDR plus PMREM is tens of MB of GPU memory and a long main-thread RGBE decode that stalls the animation loop for the very users who 'have solid setups' but share a tab with audio capture. Repo size also grows by up to 30 MB of binary per commit. K6 covers licence only. None of this is in K1-K6 or the non-functional tests.
findings.suggestion: Add a risk and a gate: per-file asset size under the Workers limit (check in CI or the build), prefer a 2K HDR or .exr to RGBE, decode and PMREM off the first-visible frames, and measure GPU memory and frame stall on a mid-range GPU in the manual test.
findings.resolution: Changed: D10 sets formats and caps each file under 20 MiB; K7 and a unit size test added; the decode stall is measured manually and the standard look keeps rendering during the load.

findings.finding: AC7 is not reliably testable or correct as written. FrameRateMonitor averages dt from the animation loop, but rAF is throttled to a fraction when the tab is hidden, on battery-saver 30 Hz modes and on 30/50 Hz displays, and delta is huge after tab return, so a fixed 'below threshold' fires falsely (K-risk noted only for SwiftShader in O3, not carried into the plan's risks). The warm-up also has to cover the renderer rebuild plus the lazy HDR swap (shader compile and PMREM hitches), or the notice fires on every first enable. The monitor also resets on each rebuild but the once-per-visit dismissal flag does not, with no AC for that interplay. AC4 and the 'no console errors' part of AC5 are likewise asserted only through a fake renderer and mocked import, so nothing proves a real enhanced frame renders.
findings.suggestion: Ignore samples with dt above a cap or while document.hidden, restart warm-up on every rebuild and asset swap, and add one e2e smoke that enables enhanced mode against the reduced asset map and checks the canvas is non-blank with no console errors.
findings.resolution: Changed: C4 ignores hidden frames and capped dt and restarts warm-up on every rebuild and asset swap; dismissal persists for the visit; an e2e smoke renders a real enhanced frame.

findings.finding: Test strategy relies on 'enhanced assets may be served at reduced size via the module's asset map' in e2e. That puts a test seam in production code and means the e2e never exercises the real asset path or the HDR parser against the committed file, so a corrupt or wrongly encoded HDR passes CI and fails only for users. The size and Lighthouse checks also never touch the lazy enhanced chunk's real RGBELoader and Reflector additions beyond 'justify in the PR'; the Total JS limit is 339.25 kB gzip and a hard fail at the end of S3 would be a late surprise.
findings.suggestion: Add a unit test that parses the real committed HDR header and checks dimensions and byte size, run npm run size after S2 (not only at the end), and keep the reduced-asset switch out of the production bundle (test-only alias or Vite define).
findings.resolution: Changed: the reduced-asset seam is removed; e2e uses the real assets; a unit test parses the committed HDR header and checks the file sizes; npm run size runs after S2.
